name: paleo_intervals_v1
frozen: 2026-10-18, at the commit that adds this file; hash in receipts/timeline_v1_freeze.txt
purpose: Source-labelled intervals for a possible future timeline layer. Each entry keeps its own source and definition; entries are never merged into one consensus date.
rules: Every number below was read in the source named with it, at the location given. Where only an abstract was read, the entry says so.
Ages are in Ga (billions of years before present). Ranges are written older first.
A present-day basemap locates Oklo as it is today. It does not depict Paleoproterozoic geography, which needs a separate paleogeographic reconstruction.

entries.label: Great Oxidation Event, as defined by Gumsley et al. 2017
entries.definition: From the onset of significant oxygenation, together with the first Paleoproterozoic global glaciation, to the end of the Lomagundi carbon-isotope excursion.
entries.end_basis: end of the Lomagundi carbon isotope excursion, ca. 2,060 Ma
entries.source: Gumsley, A.P., et al. 2017. Timing and tempo of the Great Oxidation Event. PNAS 114(8), 1811 to 1816. doi:10.1073/pnas.1608824114
entries.read: abstract only, via the Lund University research portal record; the full text was not retrieved
entries.caveat: An extended transition with oscillating oxygen, not an instant. The onset age rests on Ongeluk Formation magmatism dated 2,426 +/- 3 Ma.

entries.label: Great Oxidation Event, as framed by Craig, Kumar and Hedges 2023
entries.definition: The interval Craig et al. use for the GOE, attributed by them to Poulton et al. 2021.
entries.source: Craig, J.M., Kumar, S., and Hedges, S.B. 2023. The origin of eukaryotes and rise in complexity were synchronous with the rise in oxygen. Frontiers in Bioinformatics 3, 1233281. doi:10.3389/fbinf.2023.1233281
entries.attribution_chain: Craig et al. 2023 citing Poulton et al. 2021; Poulton et al. 2021 was not read here
entries.caveat: Not interchangeable with the Gumsley et al. 2017 definition, which runs to about 2.06 Ga.

entries.label: Oklo natural fission reactors
entries.basis: Date of the nuclear reaction, from the global amount of fissiogenic Nd (or radiogenic Th) formed per atom of uranium compared with the mean fluence received; the authors then assume all reactors share the age of 1950 Ma.
entries.source: Gauthier-Lafaye, F., Holliger, P., and Blanc, P.-L. 1996. Natural fission reactors in the Franceville basin, Gabon. Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta 60(23), 4831 to 4852
entries.corroborating_source: Gauthier-Lafaye, F. 2002. 2 billion year old natural analogs for nuclear waste disposal: the natural nuclear fission reactors in Gabon (Africa). C. R. Physique 3, 839 to 849, page 841: the age of the uranium deposit is 1950 +/- 40 Ma
entries.caveat: A dated event with its stated uncertainty. How long the reactors operated is not part of this entry.

entries.label: Origin of eukaryotes, one study's estimate
entries.location: abstract, PDF page 1; core interval 2.04 to 1.79 Ga in the results, PDF page 3
entries.caveat: One study's estimate for the origin of eukaryotes, not a consensus date and not the date of the mitochondrial endosymbiosis itself. The same paper notes earlier molecular-clock estimates spanning about 2.10 to 0.91 Ga.

derived_date_separations.label: Derived date separation between Oklo's nominal 1.95 Ga and a stated bound. Not a GOE-to-Oklo lag; it ignores Oklo's +/- 0.04 Ga and each bound's own uncertainty.

display_guidance.goe: an interval band per definition, each labelled with its source
display_guidance.oklo: a dated marker with its +/- 0.04 Ga uncertainty
display_guidance.eukaryogenesis: a labelled range from one study, with its conservative and core intervals
display_guidance.map: keep the present-day locator separate from any paleogeographic reconstruction
